entries.claim: A p-value is the probability of observing data at least as extreme as the sample, computed under a specified null model; it is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true

The 2016 ASA statement lists six principles: p-values indicate incompatibility with a model, do not measure the probability a hypothesis is true, should not decide conclusions alone, require full reporting, do not measure effect size, and are not a good standalone measure of evidence
Undisclosed flexibility in data collection and analysis lets researchers present anything as significant; a parody study made listening to a Beatles song 'reduce' reported age
entries.notes: Illustrates p-hacking, not a real effect

entries.claim: Rosenthal's fail-safe N estimates how many unpublished null results would be needed to overturn a significant meta-analytic conclusion
entries.notes: Original uses the one-tailed chi-square critical value 2.706

entries.claim: Of 100 psychology studies repeated by the Open Science Collaboration, about 36% of the original significant results were significant again
Camerer et al. replicated 18 experimental economics studies, with about 61% reproducing
Across k independent tests each at 5%, the chance of at least one false positive is 1 - 0.95^k
The uniform p-value figure and the 50/50 publish-or-file illustration are teaching schematics
entries.notes: The 50/50 split is schematic, not empirical
